newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel announces measures to cover budget gap.
newsitem.headline: Israel announces measures to cover budget gap.

text.p: The Israeli treasury announced on Monday three new taxes to close a gap of 270 million shekels in the state's 1997 budget created when parliament rejected a plan to cancel a half-point tax credit for working women.

The new measures are the cancellation of an exemption on purchase tax for air conditioners for cars, revocation of a decision to lower the price of solar oil and cancellation of a tax rebate for companies buying minivans or jeeps.
The taxes will enable the Treasury to maintain the deficit target of 2.8 percent of the gross domestic product. Israel's 1997 budget is approximately 190 billion shekels ($58.5 billion).
